summary: This is the app-side consumer coordination that HF-DB-006-SOCIAL-007 named as the blocker for tightening the post_likes / post_comments SELECT policies. Two surfaces read `post_likes` from the browser. Both reads were already self-scoped (`.eq('user_id', currentUser.id)`), so neither leaked anything, but both depend on the permissive `USING (true)` SELECT policy and neither belongs in a browser. The server-authorized replacement now exists and is proven. The required change in the artist lane's two files is a DELETION, not an integration: `GET /api/feed/posts` already returns a per-row `is_liked` computed on the caller-scoped client, and both transforms already consume it. Social has built, tested and hardened the server side; it cannot make this change itself because both files are in the artist lane's grant.
completed: `GET /api/social/post-likes?postIds=<csv>` is the canonical server-authorized batch read. 200 { success, likedPostIds: string[], degraded: false }; 400 { error: 'invalid_post_ids' | 'too_many_post_ids', maxPostIds: 50 }; 401 { error: 'Unauthorized' }. It authenticates with `checkAuth` (Bearer + cookie), reads only `.eq('user_id', viewerId)` rows, gates the requested ids on `canViewPostComments` BEFORE any like read, never imports the service-role client, and returns an explicit 500 `like_state_unavailable` instead of a false zero when a read fails.

`lib/social/post-like-state.ts` is the single implementation: bounded and de-duplicating id normalization, follow-relationship resolution in at most five queries regardless of batch size, and a `degraded` flag so 'not liked' and 'could not be determined' are distinguishable (CP-049).

Shape equivalence is proven, not argued: `__tests__/social/viewer-post-like-state.test.ts` computes the old browser read literally (`.from('post_likes').select('post_id').eq('user_id', uid).in('post_id', ids)` -> `Set<string>`) and asserts the server read returns the same Set for entitled posts, differing only by removing ids the caller may not see.

The field that makes the deletion possible is proven to survive: `normalizeFeedPostDTO` (`lib/feed/feed-post-dto.ts`) emits `is_liked: Boolean(post.is_liked)`, and a test asserts true / false / absent all round-trip.

`GET /api/feed/posts` no longer computes `is_liked` on the service-role client. `fetchViewerLikedPostIds` now receives the caller-scoped client, so the one interaction read on the feed path runs under the caller's own RLS (CP-058). The feed's own post-visibility scope in `lib/feed/feed-posts-query.ts` is unchanged and remains the gate for that surface.

The missing regression guard now exists: `__tests__/social/interaction-route-gate-inventory.test.ts` enumerates every `app/api/**/route.ts` that names an interaction table and fails unless the route calls the gate, pins its reads to the caller's own rows, or is registered with a written reason. It was proven to fail on a deliberately non-compliant route.
